newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia oil company NIS posts 1.4 bln dinar loss.
newsitem.headline: Serbia oil company NIS posts 1.4 bln dinar loss.

text.p: The Serbian oil company, Naftna Industrija Srbije (NIS), posted a 1.4 billion dinar ($251 million) loss in 1996 primarily due to uncollected claims and low derivatives prices, NIS said on Friday.

Last year the company successfully and regularly supplied the market with oil derivatives and natural gas and secured fuels for agricultural works, winter heating season and key enterprises, NIS said in a statement faxed to Reuters.

"Despite successfully supplying fuels to the economy and the population, NIS posted a loss of 1.4 billion dinars, for the most part due to uncollected claims and low prices of derivatives which have not changed for more than a year," the statement said.
The company said sufficient quantities of diesel fuel have been secured for forthcoming spring agricultural works as well as sufficient fuels for heating and major industry.

Barter deals with China for crude oil and Russia for natural gas imports have provided the needed quantities of fuels and helped revive production in many plants of the chemical, metals and other industries, whose products are exchanged for the crude and gas, the statement said.
"But the huge insolvency in NIS, conditioned primarily by the enormous debt owed to it by consumers, is threatening these arrangements," it said.

The NIS board of directors therefore calls on urgent measures to ensure repayment of outstanding debts, primarily for imported gas and oil, the statement said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
